turns.text:
You correctly noticed that the steel cans are pulled because steel contains iron, while aluminium is not attracted. 

Have you ever wondered how a hiking compass always knows which way to go? Earth itself acts like a giant magnet [c4]. A compass needle is actually just a tiny, light magnet that can spin around freely [c4]. Because opposite poles attract, the north pole of that tiny needle gets pulled toward the magnetic area in the far north [c4]. 

Why does a compass needle always point north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

Think of shining a flashlight straight down on your desk—it makes a bright, warm spot, like when your half of Earth is tilted towards the Sun and gets direct sunlight [c2].
